Tax Amounts

Tax amount reporting categories help you organize and classify the actual tax amounts collected from customers and paid to suppliers.

These categories enable accurate tax reporting by grouping similar tax transactions together for your tax returns and compliance reports.

Overview

Reporting categories for tax amounts are classification labels that organize the actual tax amounts in your transactions.

When you assign a reporting category to tax amounts, the system automatically aggregates tax collected on sales and tax paid on purchases, making it easier to prepare tax returns and calculate payment obligations.

Common Tax Categories

The most frequently used tax amount reporting categories include:

• Output tax collected - VAT/GST collected on sales to customers

• Input tax paid - VAT/GST paid on purchases from suppliers

• Import tax paid - Tax paid on imported goods at customs

• Capital goods tax - Input tax on capital asset purchases

• Partially exempt input tax - Input tax subject to partial recovery rules

• Non-deductible tax - Input tax that cannot be recovered

• Tax on exempt supplies - Special calculations for exempt supply situations

• Adjustment tax - Tax adjustments for corrections or special schemes

Benefits

Using reporting categories for tax amounts provides several advantages:

• Automatic calculation of net tax payable or refundable for each period

• Clear separation of recoverable versus non-recoverable input tax

• Simplified tax return preparation with pre-calculated category totals

• Better cash flow management through visibility of tax liabilities

• Compliance with tax authority requirements for detailed tax reporting
